text: To speak plainly, the anxieties surrounding a daughter’s future often reveal more about the parent than the child. A mother, obsessed with securing a advantageous marriage, may inadvertently communicate a disheartening message: that her daughter’s worth is contingent upon her ability to attract a suitable husband. Such a notion, though perhaps unspoken, can be profoundly damaging to a young woman’s self-esteem, fostering a dependence upon external validation and a diminished sense of her own intrinsic value. Is it not a parent’s sacred duty to instill in their child a belief in her own capabilities, to encourage her intellectual pursuits, and to prepare her for a life of independent thought and action, regardless of her marital status? To prioritize social climbing over genuine happiness is a moral failing, and a betrayal of the very trust placed in parental care.

And she lets the injury done to Jane and the contempt shown to the rest of her family aggravate this resentment in the healthiest way in the world. Still, all this does not explain her charm, which, taking beauty as a common form of all heroines, may perhaps consist in the addition to her playfulness, her wit, her affectionate and natural disposition, of a certain fearlessness very uncommon in heroines of her type and age. Nearly all of them would have been in speechless awe of the magnificent Darcy; nearly all of them would have palpitated and fluttered at the idea of proposals, even naughty ones, from the fascinating Wickham.
